subject: RFP: Inference stress profiles, emulation harness & fallback matrix
messages:
From: Jai Singh <jai.singh@aurelius.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aurelius Procurement <procurement@aurelius.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: detailed performance profiling request (latency/throughput + fallback behavior)

Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP package. We have a follow-up: our architecture and security reviewers want a granular benchmarking appendix that covers not only steady-state throughput and p99/p95 latency numbers, but also:

- how the platform behaves under synthetic bursts (10x baseline for O(30s)),
- tail-latency decomposition across concurrency and cold vs warm sessions,
- how prefix/KV cache priming affects observed latency at the application layer, and
- concrete fallback/deg mediaton behavior when a model variant is throttled or evicted (including precise routing rules and when a higher-latency fallback is chosen).

Can you provide a technical questionnaire or a worked example that documents the test harness, the exact request shapes you used, how you generated synthetic traffic, and the CSV matrix we can run against our performance team? A timeline for a short joint run (1–2 business days) would be helpful too.

Attachments: RFP-extract.pdf (we included sample Qs)

—Jai

Jai —

Appreciate the clarity. I looped in Marissa (solutions) and Evelyn (perf engineering) — they can provide the worked examples and the CSV matrix. High-level plan below; we'll attach a ready-to-run emulation harness and a fallback matrix template.

Proposed deliverables (short):
- Emulation Harness: python/Go client + k6 snippets that drive token-level and request-level mixes (will include config for burst runs and cold-start injection).
- CSV Performance Matrix: rows enumerating request shape (prompt length, context tokens, temperature, streaming vs non-streaming), concurrency buckets (1, 5, 20, 100), and measured metrics (p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), GPU utilization, observed cold-start count).
- Fallback Matrix: deterministic rules mapping capacity events to fallback model variants + expected latency delta and quality delta (we'll document when we recommend graceful degradation vs rejecting).

Timeline: we can ship the draft package by Monday EOD PDT and run a short joint 8-hour session Tues or Wed if that works.

Questions for you (so we tailor exactly):
1) Do you want synthetic requests to use your real prompt corpus or a synthetic representative mix?
2) Any hard latency SLA thresholds (e.g., p95 < 200ms for interactive flows)?

We'll attach the initial files in a follow-up message.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: detailed performance profiling request (latency/throughput + fallback behavior)

Jai / Ben —

Evelyn and I sketched the test methodology; below is the worked example for a 2-model serving scenario (primary: rdx-large-opt, fallback: rdx-large-int8):

Test harness highlights (emulation_harness.pdf attached):
- Request shapes: three buckets — short (<= 64 tokens), medium (65–512 tokens), long (513–2048 tokens). For streaming tests we emit token-by-token with 20ms inter-token pacing to emulate client-side rendering.
- Concurrency sweep: run sequentially at concurrency levels 1, 5, 20, 100, 250. Each sweep runs for 10 minutes steady-state, followed by a 30s burst at 10x baseline QPS.
- Cold-start injection: rotate 5% of requests to fresh model processes (simulate cache misses by restarting worker or toggling KV priming off) to capture cold-start tails.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (server-side, end-to-end), median and 95th percentile token emission latency (for streaming), CPU/GPU utilization, NVLink saturation, network transmit, and per-request KV lookup latency.

Fallback behavior & matrix (fallback_matrix_template.csv attached):
- Triggering conditions: 1) model on node hits 85% GPU mem or 90% SM occupancy for >30s; 2) autoscaler signals pending evictions; 3) regional capacity failure.
- Decision path: prefer same-precision quantized variant in same region -> if unavailable, route to lower-cost higher-latency variant in a different zone -> if still unavailable, employ throttling with 503 and circuit-breaker for client to retry.
- For each path we document expected p95 increase (ms), quality change (human-eval score delta), and recommended client-side retry/backoff. Example row: primary->int8 local: p95 + 45ms; primary->remote fp16: p95 + 120ms; degrade->503: recommended linear backoff 200–800ms.

CSV schema (sample columns we will provide): request_shape, concurrency, baseline_qps, burst_qps, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tok_p50_ms, tok_p95_ms, gpu_util_pct, cold_start_rate_pct, fallback_mode, fallback_lat_delta_ms, quality_delta_points

Scheduling: we can deliver the workbook and harness by EOD Monday (links below). Proposed joint runs: Tue 09/15 10:00–18:00 PDT or Wed 09/16 08:00–16:00 PDT. Pick a window and we will reserve infra.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Jai —

Attached are the artifacts we promised: aurelius_perf_matrix_v1.xlsx, runbook_emulation_harness.pdf, and fallback_matrix_template.csv. A few implementation notes and explicit commands so your perf team can reproduce locally:

1) Emulation harness quickstart (examples in runbook_emulation_harness.pdf):
- Clone: git clone https://git.redwoodinference.com/perf/emulation-harness.git
- Install: pip install -r requirements.txt (or go build ./cmd/harness)
- Run baseline sweep: ./run_harness --model rdx-large-opt --concurrency 20 --duration 600 --prompt-corpus corpus_short.json --emit-mode blocking --out metrics_baseline.csv
- Inject burst: ./run_harness --burst 10 --burst-duration 30 --burst-interval 300
- Cold-start toggle: ./run_harness --coldstart-rate 0.05 --process-restart true

2) CSV semantics: baseline_qps is observed req/s during steady window; burst_qps is peak during the 30s injection; cold_start_rate_pct measured as fraction of requests that required model process spin-up or KV miss.

3) Repro tips: for streaming token latencies enable the token trace header X-RDW-TRACE-TOKENS in the client — our harness will emit token-level latencies when present.

4) Fallback reproducibility: we include sample policies in fallback_matrix_template.csv. To emulate an eviction, run: ./fault_injector --target-gpu 0 --alloc-pressure 0.9 --evict after 60s. The policy simulator will show the routing decision timeline and expected latency delta.

We can host an ephemeral test cluster (same region as your app) for the joint run; it will include one primary and one fallback pool and we will stream live dashboards (Grafana link included in the Drive folder).

If you confirm Tue 09/15 10:00 PDT we'll reserve the infra and send a calendar invite with attendee dial-in and run objectives.

Best,

Evelyn Hart
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com
